statement: The graph shows how much water was in a tank during 35 minutes. While the amount of water was going down, the water flowed out at a steady rate. How many litres flowed out each minute?

figure.alt: A line graph of water in a tank, in litres, against time in minutes, with gridlines every 10 litres and every 5 minutes. The line rises from 0 litres at minute 0 to 60 litres at minute 10, stays at 60 litres until minute 15, falls in a straight line to 20 litres at minute 25, then rises to 80 litres at minute 35.

choices.misconception: I divided the level at the bottom of the fall, 20 litres, by the 10 minutes it took.
I worked out the rate for a part of the graph where the tank was filling, not emptying.
I gave the number of minutes the water level was falling.
I gave the total number of litres that flowed out, not the amount per minute.

hints: Find the part of the graph that slopes downwards.
Read the amount and the time where the falling part starts and where it ends. A steady rate is the change in amount divided by the time taken.
The water falls from 60 litres at minute 15 to 20 litres at minute 25.

solutions.reliable: The only falling part of the graph runs from 60 litres at minute 15 to 20 litres at minute 25. In those 10 minutes, 60 - 20 = 40 litres flowed out, so the rate was 40 / 10 = 4 litres per minute. The transferable idea: on a graph of amount against time, a rate is the change in height divided by the change in time over the part the question names.

whyOnTest: Reading a graph: find the right section, read both coordinates at each end, and turn a change in amount into a rate.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
